verdict.summary: Creating an app and testing in the sandbox takes minutes, but production keys need an approved Production Pre-Approval, a Security Review, and a QA check. Gusto says the pre-approval is not a formality, so approval is the hard part.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-3 days of active work for the sandbox build, plus the security questionnaire and evidence (more if you have no SOC 2 or ISO 27001)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 min to a sandbox connection, once you have portal access (demo data only)
verdict.approval_wait: Not stated by Gusto. Community reports range from about 1 week to 1-2 months, and they conflict.

gates.name: Sandbox / demo environment (your own app, demo data)
gates.unlocks: Create the app, get client_id and secret, and run the OAuth flow against Gusto's demo environment with demo payroll data. Use it to build and test before approval.
limits: Sandbox keys work only against the demo environment.
Demo data only is reachable; you cannot connect real Gusto customer accounts.
Scopes must be tested in the demo environment before production approval.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes to about 1 hour after portal access

gates.name: Production keys for approved partners
gates.unlocks: Real Gusto customer accounts, after Production Pre-Approval, Security Review and QA are all approved and Gusto issues production keys. Gusto's docs describe no separate test-user or invited-user tier between sandbox and production.
limits: Pre-approval is not a formality, and approval is not guaranteed.
Gusto will not provide QA support or issue production keys without both approvals.
Scopes are assigned by Gusto during review and enforced in production.
Production redirect URI changes go through Gusto support.
Demo or test accounts are not supported in production.
gates.time_to_reach: Unknown. Community reports range from about 1 week to 1-2 months.

gates.name: General availability to all Gusto customers
gates.unlocks: Launch the app to any Gusto customer. Gusto's docs describe a launch step (update your website or marketplace, publish support content) and no separate marketplace or app-store review.
limits: Gusto's docs describe no marketplace listing review, so the only documented review is the pre-approval, security review and QA in Gate 2.
Marketplace listing requirements (privacy policy, logo, demo video) are not in Gusto's docs.
gates.time_to_reach: After production keys are issued. The launch step itself is not described as a review.

steps.title: Confirm you need the App Integrations product, not Embedded Payroll
steps.detail: Use the App Integrations API at dev.gusto.com. Gusto Embedded Payroll (embedded.gusto.com) has a separate review path, so do not start there unless you are building embedded payroll. Gusto's API is currently limited to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners, so it does not cover customers connecting their own company systems to their own account.
gotchas: If you only want to connect your own Gusto company, the API may not be available to you. Confirm this with Gusto before building.
The dev.gusto.com page returned a Cloudflare challenge during research, so the screens below were not checked directly.

steps.title: Create a Developer Portal account and an organization
steps.detail: Sign up for a Developer Portal account at dev.gusto.com. Gusto's recommended order is to create the account, onboard to the sandbox, and file the Production Pre-Approval as early as possible, ideally before building. Answer 'No' to 'Are you building embedded payroll?' unless that is your product.
gotchas: Research did not confirm whether an organization must be created before applications, or whether a paid plan or business verification is needed. Check this when you sign up.
File Production Pre-Approval early, because Gusto gives no timeline and community reports differ.

steps.title: Create the application and add the Redirect URI
steps.detail: In the Developer Portal, create a new application in the Applications area and give it a name. Add the redirect URI exactly as shown in your Composio auth config, then save. Gusto generates a client_id and client secret for the app.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Wildcard URIs and URIs with fragments (#) are not allowed. Add each redirect as a separate entry on the same application, not as a new application.
Demo redirects can be edited on the Applications tab. Production redirect changes must go through Gusto support, so get the value right before you go to production.
Research did not verify the portal screen labels. Use the labels you see on screen.

steps.title: Record the client credentials and check endpoints
steps.detail: Store client_id and client_secret in your secret manager, not in code. Check the endpoints against Gusto's OIDC discovery document before you rely on Composio's defaults, because the two sources disagree.
gotchas: The authorization endpoint returned a Cloudflare challenge during research, even for a fake client_id. It did not show how unknown clients are rejected, so verify with a real sandbox client_id.

steps.title: Run a sandbox authorization with an admin account
steps.detail: Sign in to the sandbox as a primary admin or full-access admin and complete the OAuth flow from your app. Only those admin types can authorize a new application. Exchange the code at the token endpoint with client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code and grant_type.
gotchas: The authorization code expires after 10 minutes.
The redirect_uri in the request must be percent-encoded and match the registered URI exactly.
Access tokens expire 2 hours after issue. Each refresh token can be used once to get a new access and refresh token pair, so store the new refresh token each time.

steps.title: Settle the scopes you need and check the granted scopes
steps.detail: List the minimum scopes your use case needs and write a short justification for each. Gusto uses the scopes you request to assign scopes during review, so the list must match the use case. After a sandbox sign-in, check the granted scopes in the Developer Portal.
gotchas: employees:read and payrolls:read did not appear by name in the OIDC sample, so confirm them with Gusto before you rely on them.
Calls outside the granted scopes are rejected in production.
Extra scopes after go-live are requested by email to Gusto support. A community guide mentions an 'Application Scope Update' form option, which was not verified.

steps.title: Complete the Production Pre-Approval questionnaire
steps.detail: Fill in the Production Pre-Approval application. Gusto uses the same questionnaire for the pre-approval and the security review, so answer it completely. The form is hosted on Qualtrics and was not read during research, so the questions below are inferred from the security review requirements.
gotchas: Pre-approval is not a formality and approval is not guaranteed.
The questionnaire is the intake for the security review, so answers given here will be used again.

steps.title: Prepare security evidence
steps.detail: Draft the privacy, incident-response and data-retention policies and a description of your controls. Use these to answer the questionnaire. If you hold a current SOC 2 Type 2 or ISO 27001 report, attach it. Also gather penetration test reports and name a security contact and an incident-response contact.
gotchas: Without a formal audit, Gusto asks for descriptions of many controls, including MFA, encryption, vulnerability management and brute-force protection.
A community guide lists SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 as the acceptable certifications, but Gusto's own page is the authority.
Gusto's security review is run with a third party, VISO Trust (community report), and may ask for more documents.

steps.title: Wait for the Partnerships review
steps.detail: Gusto's Partnerships team reviews your application. If it is approved, Gusto's GRC team starts the security review. Direct applicants get next steps by email. Gusto gives no timeline.
gotchas: Community timelines conflict: about 1-2 weeks for pre-approval (Lansweeper), at least 2 weeks with no fast track (Finch), about 1 week for the security review (Merge), and about 1-2 months overall (Pipedream).
Gusto's docs describe no fast-track process.

steps.title: Answer the security review and complete the Partner Checklist
steps.detail: After pre-approval, you can access the Partner Checklist. Copy it, use it to scope the build, complete it, and share it with Gusto. Respond to any follow-up requests from the GRC team during the security review.
gotchas: The Partner Checklist is available only after pre-approval is approved.
Gusto may ask for more documents or clarification during the security review.

steps.title: Pass QA and receive production keys
steps.detail: Gusto runs a quality review of the built integration before it issues production keys. Gusto will not issue production keys without the pre-approval and security review both approved. Once you have them, switch the app from demo to production credentials.
gotchas: Gusto cannot provide QA support or production keys without both approvals.
Demo or test accounts are not supported in production, so test with real customer accounts only after go-live.

steps.title: Launch to customers and plan for rate limits
steps.detail: Move the build to production and make it available to customers. Update your website or marketplace and publish support content. Design for the documented rate limit of 200 requests per minute per access token, and expect 429 responses above that.
gotchas: Gusto's docs describe no separate marketplace listing review, but listing requirements (privacy policy, logo, demo video) are not documented.
Redirect URI changes after launch go through Gusto support.

requirements.detail: Required to create an app. Answer 'No' to the embedded payroll question unless you are building embedded payroll.

requirements.item: At least one redirect URI on the application
requirements.detail: Must match the Composio callback exactly. No wildcards or fragments. Percent-encode when sending.
Sandbox keys work only against the demo environment with demo data.

requirements.item: Primary or full-access admin to authorize
requirements.detail: Only these admin types can enable and authenticate a new application's access. Multi-company admins must run the flow per company.
Must be approved before Gusto will provide QA support or production keys. Not a formality.
Run by Gusto's GRC team after pre-approval. Pre-approval answers usually suffice. Expect SOC 2 Type 2 or ISO 27001 evidence, or a full controls description if you have no audit.
Granted only after pre-approval. Completed and shared with Gusto before production keys are issued.

requirements.item: Scopes tested in demo and enforced in production
requirements.detail: Gusto assigns scopes during review. Calls outside granted scopes are rejected.

requirements.item: No demo or test accounts in production
requirements.detail: Production connects real customer accounts only.

blockers.symptom: Production Pre-Approval or Security Review is declined or stalls, so no production keys are issued.
blockers.cause: Gusto says pre-approval is not a formality and gates production access. Without approval, Gusto will not provide QA support or production keys.
blockers.fix: File the pre-approval early. Prepare SOC 2 Type 2 or ISO 27001 evidence, or a full control description, before you file. Ask Gusto what is missing if it stalls.
blockers.contact: Gusto Partnerships team, through the Developer Portal or support channel

blockers.symptom: You want to connect only your own Gusto company through the API and cannot get API access.
blockers.cause: Gusto does not currently support API access for customers connecting their own systems to their own account. The API is limited to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners.
blockers.fix: Confirm eligibility with Gusto before building. Do not plan on your own company's production data unless Gusto confirms access.

blockers.symptom: The app only reaches demo payroll data, not real companies.
blockers.cause: New integrations stay in the demo environment until they are reviewed and approved for production.
blockers.fix: Build and test in the sandbox, then complete Gate 2 before testing with real customer data.

blockers.symptom: Requested scopes (for example employees:read or payrolls:read) are not granted in production.
blockers.cause: Gusto assigns scopes during review based on the use case. Composio's default scopes were not confirmed by Gusto's OIDC sample.
blockers.fix: Confirm the scope names in the sandbox and request only what your use case needs. Justify each scope in your review answers.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Gusto, so you must register your own Gusto app and enter its client_id and secret in Composio. Sandbox work can start before approval. Real customer accounts need Gusto's production keys, which need an approved Production Pre-Approval and Security Review. Composio's default authorization URL (api.gusto.com) differs from the discovery document (app.gusto.com), so verify it. Composio's default scopes are unverified in production.

open_questions: Gusto's own pages give no review timeline. The 1-2 week, at-least-2-week, about-1-week and 1-2 month figures come from community sources and conflict with each other.
Gusto's Production Pre-Approval form (hosted on Qualtrics), the Partner Checklist and the Developer Terms were not read directly.
Whether Composio's default scopes (companies:read, employees:read, payrolls:read) are granted in production is unverified. The OIDC sample does not name employees:read or payrolls:read.

Composio's default redirect (backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) differs from the callback used in the probe (backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback). Use the exact callback shown in your Composio auth config.
The Developer Portal sits behind a Cloudflare challenge. Application-creation screens, business verification, admin roles, whether an organization is required, and any paid plan were not verified.
Composio's authorization URL (api.gusto.com/oauth/authorize) differs from the discovery document (app.gusto.com/oauth/authorize). Confirm which one Gusto accepts for your client_id.
Rate limits for new or unreviewed apps are not documented. The 200 requests per minute limit is the only documented limit.
PKCE support is unconfirmed. The OIDC document lists no PKCE methods, and the OAuth2 doc describes only the client-secret code flow.
Gusto's docs describe no test-user or invited-user tier between sandbox and production, so the Gate 2 label is an approximation.
Marketplace or app-directory listing requirements are not described in Gusto's docs. The launch step is the closest documented equivalent.
Refresh-token behaviour on reuse (after a single use) is not spelled out.
